summary: If this[76] (element count) is positive, iterates count times over the sub-object array at this[77] with a 316-byte stride. For each of three index fields in the current entry (offsets +292 parent, +288 child, +296 sibling from the entry base): an index of -1 or >= count causes the corresponding pointer field (+272 parent, +268 child, +276 sibling) to be zeroed and the index reset to -1; otherwise the pointer field is set to the array base plus 316 * index, remapping array-index references into direct pointers.

local_names.array: this[77] sub-object array base at offset 0x134

operations.description: Load count = this[76]; only proceed with the remapping loop when count > 0.
Iterate from index 0 up to count-1, advancing a running byte offset by 316 (sub-object stride) each pass over the array base this[77].
For the parent-index field at entry offset +292: if the index is -1 or >= count, write 0 to the parent-pointer field at +272 and reset the index field at +292 to -1.
For the parent-index field at entry offset +292 with a valid index: write array base + 316 * index to the parent-pointer field at +272.
For the child-index field at entry offset +288: if the index is -1 or >= count, write 0 to the child-pointer field at +268 and reset the index field at +288 to -1.
For the child-index field at entry offset +288 with a valid index: write array base + 316 * index to the child-pointer field at +268.
For the sibling-index field at entry offset +296: if the index is -1 or >= count, write 0 to the sibling-pointer field at +276 and reset the index field at +296 to -1.
For the sibling-index field at entry offset +296 with a valid index: write array base + 316 * index to the sibling-pointer field at +276.

unresolved: Semantic meaning of the three remapped links (parent/child/sibling at +272/+268/+276 and indices at +292/+288/+296) is a DERIVED reading; no evidence in the packet names them.
Entry-offset +268/+272/+276 and +288/+292/+296 are derived from the raw source and have no dedicated evidence refs; the packet only exposes base this[77] and count this[76].
Concrete sub-object type (316-byte stride) is unknown.
Why invalid indices are reset to -1 while the pointer is zeroed (rather than both being consistent) is unexplained.
